gaps.reason: The extracted facts only mention negative cash flows as a risk; no actual cash flow from operations, investing, or financing is provided in the digest.

beats.beat: Contracts are won through a competitive tender process. The client floats a tender, a pre-bid meeting is held, and the job is awarded to the lowest bidder. The contractor then deposits a performance guarantee.
Revenue is highly concentrated: Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the order book as of the latest period.
Top customers — including Western Railway, Central Railway, Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, MMRDA, and others — accounted for 57% of total revenue in FY2018.
The second segment, ready-mix concrete (RMC), provides manufacturing revenue but its split is not disclosed separately in the filing.

The company cites quality, transparency, long-standing client relationships (since 2006 with Western Railway), use of box-pushing technique, experienced management, and a healthy order book as competitive strengths.

business.heading: What the company does
business.purpose: Explain the business model: contract bidding, two revenue streams, client concentration, and competitive strengths.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations fell from ₹90.21 crore in FY2015 to ₹60.53 crore in FY2018, a decline of about 33% over three years. The earlier peak was ₹90.21 crore (FY2015); FY2014 was ₹86.61 crore.
Net profit after adjustments was volatile: ₹0.96 crore in FY2014, ₹0.78 crore in FY2015, ₹0.33 crore in FY2016, ₹0.16 crore in FY2017, and a sharp jump to ₹3.15 crore in FY2018.
EBITDA (Profit before interest, depreciation and tax) ranged from ₹7.83 crore (FY2016) to ₹9.46 crore (FY2015). In FY2018 it was ₹9.29 crore.
Long-term borrowings declined from ₹5.87 crore in FY2014 to ₹1.33 crore in FY2018, but short-term borrowings rose from ₹30.82 crore to ₹35.37 crore over the same period.
The company reported negative cash flows in recent years, which it identifies as a risk factor for its business.

financials.heading: Financial performance (₹ crore)
financials.purpose: Present revenue, PAT, EBITDA, debt, and cash flow trends across the reported periods (FY2014–FY2018).

beats.beat: Promoter Amit Bholanath Mishra holds 74,95,476 equity shares, constituting 90.949% of the pre-issue paid-up capital. Other directors hold only 300 shares each.
Key management personnel include CFO Anchal Pachori (age 28, CA) and Company Secretary Mohit Soni (age 26, ACS).
Related-party transactions in FY2018: loans from KMP/board ₹68.4 lakh, director remuneration ₹57.7 lakh, and outstanding payables to related parties ₹324.3 lakh as on March 31, 2018.
Two companies promoted by Amit Bholanath Mishra (Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited) were struck off by the ROC in March 2016 due to non-operation.
No independent monitoring agency has been appointed for fund utilisation; the company will rely on its audit committee.
There are no criminal cases filed against the directors, and they are not on the RBI list of willful defaulters.

governance.heading: Ownership and governance
governance.purpose: Describe the promoter holding, board composition, related-party transactions, and any red flags from the filing.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector contributes roughly 8% to India’s GDP and is highly fragmented with many unorganized players.
Key demand drivers include government flagship programs (Smart Cities, AMRUT, Make in India), easing of FDI norms in 15 sectors, and rising urbanization and disposable income.
India is projected to need US$ 1 trillion in infrastructure investment by 2022; the logistics sector is growing at a CAGR of 10.5% (2017–2020).
Competition comes from both organized and unorganized players; the market is working-capital-intensive and subject to slow government project execution and policy changes.

industry.heading: Industry and market
industry.purpose: Describe the construction/infrastructure sector, its size, growth drivers, competition, and the headwinds identified in the filing.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild is an infrastructure construction company that also operates a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant, focused on government and public-sector projects in and around Mumbai.
The company works in two segments: building infrastructure (railways, bridges, roads) and manufacturing RMC at a facility in Kashimira, Thane.
It is issuing 44,28,000 new equity shares of ₹10 each at a price to be determined; all proceeds go to the company (no offer-for-sale).
The main use of the proceeds is ₹1,130 lakhs (₹11.30 crore) for working capital, with the remainder for general corporate purposes.
The sole promoter, Amit Bholanath Mishra, controls 74,95,476 equity shares (90.949% of pre-issue capital).

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: A B Infrabuild Limited is a Mumbai-based infrastructure contractor and ready-mix concrete manufacturer, raising a fresh equity issue primarily to fund working capital. Its sole promoter holds nearly 91% pre-issue.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of face value ₹10 each. The price band will be determined later. There is no offer for sale component.
Net proceeds after issue expenses are to be used for: (i) meeting working capital requirements – ₹1,130 lakhs; (ii) general corporate purposes – amount not disclosed.
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited; the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
The company has not appointed an independent agency to appraise the project and will rely on internal monitoring by the audit committee.

offer.heading: The IPO structure
offer.purpose: Detail the issue size, components, use of proceeds, and lead manager.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: Indian Railways (primarily Western Railway) contributed 57% of revenue in FY2018. Loss of this client would severely affect revenue and profitability.
Negative cash flows in recent years could impair the company’s ability to fund operations and working capital needs.
Unsecured loans of ₹405.02 lakh as on March 31, 2018 are repayable on demand. A sudden repayment call could strain liquidity.
The company has entered into significant related-party transactions and may continue to do so, which could raise governance concerns.
Contracts in the order book may be cancelled, adjusted, or suspended by clients, meaning the order book is not a guaranteed indicator of future revenue.

risks.heading: Material risks from the filing
risks.purpose: List the top 3-5 specific risks disclosed in the DRHP, each with a direct citation.

beats.beat: The company's EPS (basic) improved from ₹1.31 in FY2016 to ₹0.63 in FY2017 and ₹12.59 in FY2018. Return on Net Worth (RoNW) moved from 4.14% to 1.97% and then 28.14% over the same years.

The filing does not name specific peer companies or provide their valuation multiples. It states that the issue price is justified based on the above accounting ratios, but no comparative table is available.
Without disclosed peer data, a market-based valuation range using competitor multiples cannot be computed from the filing.
